hook.text: In 2006, a Yahoo engineer named Doug Cutting released an open-source project named after his son's toy elephant.

buildup.text: Hadoop implemented Google's ideas: a distributed file system plus a MapReduce processing engine.

discovery.text: For the first time, anyone could process petabytes of data on clusters of cheap commodity hardware.

twist.text: Hadoop was powerful but painful — low-level Java code, slow batch jobs, and no interactive queries.

climax.text: Despite its flaws, Hadoop proved that distributed processing at massive scale was achievable by anyone.

punchline.text: A toy elephant's name changed data forever.
